claims.explanation: Puromycin is a tRNA mimic that incorporates into nascent polypeptides causing premature chain termination and ribosome stalling; selectivity likely reflects differences in protein synthesis load, ribosome composition, and stress/apoptotic priming. Lines with high ribosome biogenesis and mTOR/translation activity (e.g., EGFR-mutant, PIK3CA-mutant, PTEN-loss, MYC-amplified) are more sensitive, while lines with low translation or intact stress adaptation are protected. The virtual-cell signature (proteasome/ubiquitin and stress-granule genes) supports translation-stress and proteotoxic responses as the downstream selective mechanism.

features.basis: EGFR-mutant NSCLC lines (NCIH1650, HCC4006, KYSE270) are among the most killed; EGFR drives high mTOR-dependent translation
PTEN loss (ZR751, UACC62, HEC265, KALS1, FTC133) activates PI3K/mTOR and translation, increasing puromycin incorporation
PIK3CA-mutant lines (HGC27, SNU840, MKN1, SNUC5) show high selective killing, consistent with mTOR-driven translation
BRAF-mutant melanoma/colorectal lines (UACC62, K029AX, IGR37, HEC265, SNUC5) are enriched among sensitive lines
TP53 mutation is nearly universal in both sensitive and resistant lines, so it is not selective; loss of p53-mediated apoptosis may blunt puromycin killing in some contexts
SF3B1-mutant lines (UO31, HCC95) are among the least affected, suggesting altered splicing reduces dependence on translation or stress response
NRAS-mutant lines (IPC298, KU1919) are in the least-affected group, possibly reflecting lower translation or adaptive resistance
NCIH1437 (MAP2K1-mutant) is among the least affected, suggesting MAPK pathway activation without high translation load is protective
MYC-driven ribosome biogenesis and translation would increase puromycin incorporation and toxicity (mechanistic inference)
RPL11 is a puromycin target and ribosomal stress sensor; high expression may increase drug incorporation and p53-independent stress
DDIT4 downregulation in the virtual cell (HCC515) suggests mTOR release; high DDIT4 would restrain translation and protect from puromycin
BIRC5 (survivin) downregulation in the virtual cell indicates mitotic/apoptotic priming that may enhance puromycin killing
